capability: Chrysalis Homecoming (CFS-023) constitutional anchoring repair — live execution attempt against Aletheon
milestone: The generic anchoring repair (services/agents/repairDelegationAnchor.ts) was invoked live against Aletheon and correctly refused, precisely locating the blocking condition as a pre-existing, sponsor-side identity-consolidation gap rather than a defect in the repair itself
problem: The generic constitutional-anchoring repair built and tested this session (RES/CI records from earlier the same day) was invoked live by the operator against Aletheon: POST /api/homecoming/agent/repair-anchor { delegate: 'aletheon' }. It returned { ok: false, error: 'principal_unresolved', detail: 'lineage_incomplete' } rather than anchoring the delegate. This is the repair's own sibling-root disambiguation rule (reused verbatim from services/identity/passportPrincipal.ts::resolveAuthUserForKybe) firing as designed: devagent@qripto's Kybe lineage resolves to MORE THAN ONE distinct auth_user_id across sibling root_identity rows, which is exactly the ambiguity that rule refuses to resolve by guessing.
observedFailure: The repair's refusal is CORRECT behaviour, not a defect — confirmed by design and by the canary suite (tests/agent-delegation-anchor-repair.test.ts's 'sibling-root determinism' describe block already exercises exactly this refusal path with a mocked lineage_incomplete result).

The underlying condition is a genuine, pre-existing gap: passportPrincipal.ts's own header comment names it directly — 'two auth users under one personhood is precisely what Passport consolidation (Amendment A §A.5) exists to reconcile. Until it ships, refuse rather than choose.' Amendment A §A.5 has not shipped as of this record.

This gap predates and is unrelated to Aletheon's own genesis or the anchoring repair built this session. It is a property of the SPONSOR's own account lineage (devagent@qripto), not of Aletheon's agent_root_identity or agent_persona rows, which remain exactly as they were (untouched — the repair made no writes on this attempt, confirmed by its own no-write-on-refusal design).
rootCauses: The sponsor persona devagent@qripto has, at the database level, more than one root_identity row sharing its Kybe (personhood) lineage but resolving to different Supabase auth_user_id values — the exact case Passport consolidation (§A.5) was chartered to reconcile, which has not yet been built.

Because the repair (correctly) reuses the platform's existing, deliberately conservative disambiguation rule rather than inventing a laxer one for this occasion, it inherits that rule's refusal posture. This is the intended, governed behaviour — the alternative (silently picking one sibling root) would risk anchoring Aletheon to the WRONG principal identity, an error with real constitutional-continuity consequences that a refusal avoids entirely.
resolution: No repair code change is proposed or needed — the refusal is the repair functioning correctly, evidenced by its own test suite already covering this exact path before the live attempt occurred.

The blocking condition is out of scope for the Aletheon anchoring repair to resolve: it is a sponsor-account identity-consolidation question, not a Homecoming delegate question. Resolving it requires either (a) Amendment A §A.5's consolidation mechanism, not yet built, or (b) a direct, human-supervised inspection of the sponsor's sibling root_identity rows to determine whether they represent the same human via two login methods (benign) or a genuine data-integrity question — read-only SQL for this inspection was provided to the operator, not executed by this session (no live DB access).

Per operator's closeout directive ('do not open new conceptual work unless a blocking contradiction appears'): this IS a blocking contradiction for Aletheon's anchoring specifically, so it is reported and Aletheon-specific work stops here, rather than building a Passport-consolidation feature unprompted — that would be new, unscoped, platform-wide work far beyond this session's mandate.
rejectedApproaches: Relaxing resolveAuthUserForKybe's refusal rule (e.g., picking the most-recently-created sibling root, or the one with an active kyc_status) to let the Aletheon repair proceed. Rejected: this would silently choose a principal identity on ambiguous grounds, exactly the failure mode the existing rule exists to prevent, and would apply platform-wide to every future caller of that shared function, not just this one case.

Building an Aletheon-specific bypass or a one-off consolidation shortcut inside the anchoring repair. Rejected per the operator's own repeated instruction across this session: implement the smallest GENERIC resolution at the personhood layer, never an Aletheon-specific branch — the same discipline that produced resolvePassportPrincipalById in the first place forbids special-casing this failure away.
